text: I see you are experiencing right leg weakness, an unsteady gait with multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To understand the root cause, has anyone noticed any changes in your handwriting, speech, or muscle stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Cerebral Artery Stroke (Thalamic/Vermis involvement) with superimposed delirium.

I have noted the acute onset of right leg weakness and gait instability over one week, alongside a progressive decline in cognition and behavior over six months. Given the combination of focal motor deficits and recent acute falls, I must rule out an acute vascular event or compressive lesion. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Axial T2/FLAIR and DWI sequences.
